topics.title: Act I: The Magic, and the Map

concepts.title: Retrieval as the Epistemic Bottleneck
concepts.summary: Organisations fail not from lack of information but lack of retrievability — and a RAG generator can only be as truthful as the evidence placed before it.

concepts.title: Semantic vs Lexical Search & the Bi-Encoder
concepts.summary: Lexical search matches strings; semantic search matches meaning rendered as position in a vector space — the bi-encoder picture, and the three query families where they diverge.

concepts.title: The Map: Fourteen Instruments, One Pipeline
concepts.summary: The course is a single pipeline from raw document to measured, trustworthy answer — each week adds one instrument, and each instrument answers a specific pathology of naive RAG.

topics.title: Act II: How the Machine Sees

concepts.title: Language Models & the Seq2Seq Scaffold
concepts.summary: A language model factorises sequence probability into next-token predictions; seq2seq splits understanding (encoder) from speaking (decoder) — and RAG systems use two different models for the two jobs.

concepts.title: Attention: From Bahdanau's Alignment to 'All You Need'
concepts.summary: Attention began as a cure for the seq2seq bottleneck — soft alignment over encoder states — and the transformer made alignment the whole machine: a soft, differentiable lookup over keys and values.

concepts.title: Machines Think in 'Machinese': Vectors & Cosine Similarity
concepts.summary: The native currency of machine cognition is proximity, similarity, and probability — the distributional hypothesis, word2vec's directions of meaning, and why cosine similarity is the workhorse of retrieval.

concepts.title: Polysemy: One Word, Many Points
concepts.summary: Static embeddings strand ambiguous words between clusters; contextual embeddings read the sentence and move the point — and inside models, superposition is the same pressure one level deeper.

concepts.title: Querying Into the Model: LARQL & the Residual Stream
concepts.summary: A model's knowledge is geometry in its weights, and tools like LARQL can query it almost like a database — the doorway to mechanistic interpretability, and why a RAG engineer should never treat the model as an oracle.

topics.title: Act III: The Geometry of Meaning

concepts.title: Embeddings as Points in High-Dimensional Space
concepts.summary: An embedding model maps text to points in ℝᵈ where meaning is distributed holographically across coordinates; retrieval is nearest-neighbour search, made fast by ANN indexes like HNSW.

concepts.title: The Curse of Dimensionality
concepts.summary: As dimension grows, volume explodes, points become hopelessly sparse, and volume flees to the corners — the inscribed ball vanishes, naive spatial indexes degrade, and 'nearest' comes under pressure.

concepts.title: Concentration of Measure
concepts.summary: In high dimensions randomness becomes oddly orderly — pairwise distances concentrate, random vectors become nearly orthogonal, and useful structure must be put there by learning.

concepts.title: Anisotropy vs Isotropy: A Demonstration
concepts.summary: Concentration of measure is a property of the space; anisotropy is a property of the learned distribution within it — raw BERT embeddings crowd into a narrow cone, while retrieval-trained embeddings spread out and separate.

concepts.title: Naive RAG and Its Pathologies
concepts.summary: The simplest possible RAG system — embed, store, retrieve top-k, paste into the prompt — and a geometry-grounded catalogue of exactly how and why it fails.

topics.title: Act I: The Shape of a Decision

concepts.title: Softmax, Built by Hand — and the Temperature Knob
concepts.summary: The softmax turns a fistful of raw logits into a lawful probability distribution by exponentiating and normalizing, and one hidden knob, temperature, dials the result between a hard snap and a shrug without ever changing what the machine prefers.

concepts.title: Surprise, Negative Log-Likelihood, and the Cross-Entropy Family
concepts.summary: Surprise is a decreasing function of the probability you assigned to what actually happened, and the logarithm is the repair that sends certainty to zero surprise — from there, entropy, cross-entropy, and perplexity are just this one quantity, averaged and re-dressed.

concepts.title: Maximum Likelihood, the Gradient of Cross-Entropy, and Calibration
concepts.summary: Softmax paired with negative log-likelihood yields a gradient of disarming simplicity, predicted minus actual, and that same logarithm turns out to be forced rather than chosen — the only continuous repair that keeps a billion-term likelihood product computable at all.

topics.title: Act II: The Lookup That Learns

concepts.title: Attention as Fuzzy Dictionary Lookup: Four Exercises
concepts.summary: Attention is the fuzzy lookup you already perform every time you type a misspelled word into a dictionary — distribute a unit of attention over the nearby known words, weighted by proximity, and read off a blended meaning.

concepts.title: Tokenization, and Why Meaning Needs a Manifold
concepts.summary: A word is not the natural atom of text — a tokenizer chops it into subword pieces first — and machines must represent those pieces as points on a continuous manifold because gradient descent only ever makes infinitesimal moves.

concepts.title: Self-Attention Revisited: Query, Key, Value, and a Worked Example
concepts.summary: A word resolves its own ambiguity by scoring a query formed from itself against the keys of its sentence-mates and reading back a softmax-weighted blend of their values — the fuzzy dictionary lookup, turned inward and made differentiable.

concepts.title: Pooling, Layers, and the Residual Stream: From Tokens to One Vector
concepts.summary: Self-attention gives one contextual vector per token, but a search index wants one vector per chunk — mean-pooling bridges the gap, and stacking many attention layers over a residual stream is how that vector's meaning deepens.

concepts.title: Masked Language Modelling: Guess the Missing Word
concepts.summary: BERT's training objective is the card game of guessing a blanked-out word, scored by exactly the negative log-likelihood built this morning — and a model that consistently wins that game across billions of novel sentences must have learned something real about language.

topics.title: Act III: The Geometry of Belief

concepts.title: Anisotropy and Its Cure: Triplet Loss and InfoNCE
concepts.summary: A model trained only to predict words learns a representation crammed into a narrow cone, because attraction with no repulsion has one stable end state — contrastive learning supplies the missing repulsive force, and its modern form, InfoNCE, is the softmax and negative log-likelihood again, now sculpting the globe itself.

concepts.title: Bi-Encoders, Cross-Encoders, and the Unit Sphere
concepts.summary: There are exactly two ways to ask a BERT-like model how related two texts are, and the trade between them organizes the architecture of every retrieval system; both rely on cosine similarity, which is a dot product in disguise once vectors are normalized onto the unit sphere.

concepts.title: Search as Motion on a Curved Surface: KL Divergence, HNSW, and CLIP
concepts.summary: Once meaning is geometry, search is navigation across a curved surface — the same view that reveals KL divergence as the natural distance between beliefs, explains why a vector database walks a graph instead of scanning every point, and lets a sentence retrieve a photograph through CLIP's shared space.

weeks.title: Measuring the Size of Thoughts: To Chunk, or Not to Chunk?

topics.title: Act I: The First Cut Is the Deepest

concepts.title: The First Projection Is Irreversible
concepts.summary: Chunking is not preprocessing but the first lossy projection in the pipeline, and what the encoder never sees, the generator can never recover.

concepts.title: Why We Chunk: Atoms of Thought
concepts.summary: A document is an ensemble of thoughts, not one thought, and mixing two orthogonal ones in a single embedding creates a phantom point that answers neither.

concepts.title: The Boundary Problem and the 512-Token Default
concepts.summary: A document is a continuous stream of meaning with no ground-truth boundary, and the industry's default of 512 tokens is a baseline for expedience, not a considered choice.

topics.title: Act II: A Field Guide to What Chunking Destroys

concepts.title: Endophora and Broken References
concepts.summary: Language refers to itself through anaphora and cataphora, and cutting a chunk boundary between a pronoun and its antecedent leaves the fragment fluent but incoherent.

concepts.title: Discourse Structure and the Severing of Relations
concepts.summary: Documents are trees of rhetorical relations, not sequences of independent sentences, and severing them yields chunks that read true but mean the opposite of the whole.

concepts.title: The Negation Trap and Scope Failures
concepts.summary: Scope failures do not just lose information, they invert it, and presupposition accommodation silently promotes a hedged hypothesis to certainty with no error signal at all.

concepts.title: Lexical Cohesion and Definition–Use Chains
concepts.summary: Documents cohere through a sustained field of related words, and chunking dissolves that field, orphaning both disambiguating terms and legal definitions from their uses.

concepts.title: Bridging Inference and Genre Blindness
concepts.summary: Some connections have nothing explicit to sever, and a uniform chunk size ignores that a contract, a novel, and a paper carry information at wildly different densities.

concepts.title: Pathologies in Embedding Space
concepts.summary: A chunk's embedding is the centroid of its content, so packing distinct thoughts into one chunk produces a phantom vector near none of them, and anisotropy makes it worse.

topics.title: Act III: Two Roads — Better Chunking, or No Chunking?

concepts.title: A Taxonomy of Chunking Strategies
concepts.summary: From fixed-size to recursive to semantic to hierarchical chunking, each strategy improves where we cut but none heals what the cut severs.

concepts.title: Re-Contextualization: Contextual and Late Chunking
concepts.summary: Rather than inflate chunks, restore context dynamically — contextual chunking repairs in text space with an LLM-written preface, while late chunking repairs in latent space by chunking after encoding.

concepts.title: A Practical Pipeline
concepts.summary: The best systems layer markup, semantic hierarchy, contextualization, and late chunking as defense in depth, then let a tournament — not dogma — decide what to keep.

concepts.title: Road Two: Are We Barking Up the Wrong Tree?
concepts.summary: Every chunking strategy shares the hidden premise that we should parse text at all, and vision-language models like ColPali suggest that for layout-rich documents, the page image is the better semantic unit.

weeks.title: The Understudy: Search-Native Text & Derivative Artifacts

topics.title: Act I: The Purpose Problem

concepts.title: The Understudy: When the Text You Search Is Not the Text You Show
concepts.summary: For three weeks we indexed the author's own words; this week we manufacture new text written for the searcher, search that instead, and show the reader the original.

concepts.title: Meera and Ravi: Two Ways to Prepare for an Exam
concepts.summary: A story about two exam-takers shows that representation follows purpose, and that a textbook built for understanding is the wrong shape for a system that must instantly match a query to an answer.

concepts.title: Every Text Wears a Costume
concepts.summary: The same underlying fact is dressed differently for peer reviewers, adversaries, shareholders, and everyone else, and a user's naked query matches none of the costumes well.

concepts.title: The Central Provocation and the Geometry of Dilution
concepts.summary: The design principle for the rest of the week, plus the geometric reason it is necessary — a multi-claim paragraph embeds near the average of its claims, which dilutes its similarity to any one pointed query.

topics.title: Act II: The Derivative Artifacts — and the Proof

concepts.title: Factoids: Distilling the Atoms of Meaning
concepts.summary: A factoid is the smallest textual unit that still means something, the semantic molecule left after you pry every self-contained claim loose from a paragraph.

concepts.title: The PRML Bake-Off: Measuring the Difference
concepts.summary: A live experiment on Bishop's PRML textbook indexes raw chunks against factoids and QA pairs and asks why polynomial regression overfits, turning the week's claim from assertion into measurement.

concepts.title: The Centroid Tug-of-War: Feeling the Geometry
concepts.summary: A physical classroom demonstration with five students as fact-vertices and one marooned at their centroid makes the dilution inequality visible as a shrinking walk across the floor.

concepts.title: Passage Rewrites: The Source's Understudy
concepts.summary: A passage rewrite reformulates a hostile span into plain search-friendly language while the original clause remains the only thing ever shown to the reader or cited to the model.

concepts.title: QA Pairs: Planting Query-Shaped Objects
concepts.summary: Generating candidate questions per chunk turns retrieval into a same-genre match, question against question, instead of a cross-genre one, and a pointer back to the source keeps the artifact honest.

concepts.title: The Core Pattern: Retrieve the Derivative, Generate from the Source
concepts.summary: One pattern unifies every artifact in the toolkit — win the retrieval with the derivative but always generate and cite from the original, which bounds a bad derivative's damage to a missed retrieval, never a fabricated citation.

topics.title: Act III: Altitude — Summaries, RAPTOR, and the Corpus

concepts.title: Abstractive Summarization: Trading Detail for Altitude
concepts.summary: A summary is not a compression but a change of altitude, trading fine detail for large-scale structure and answering the thematic queries no single chunk can.

concepts.title: RAPTOR: Building the Zoom Lens
concepts.summary: RAPTOR gives summarization recursive structure, clustering and summarizing chunks over and over until a document becomes a tree searchable at every level of magnification.

concepts.title: From One Book to a Library: RAPTOR's Definitive Articles
concepts.summary: Run RAPTOR over a corpus rather than a document and its upper nodes stop summarizing one source, instead synthesizing a canonical answer across every document that touches the topic.

weeks.title: When the Library Becomes a City: GraphRAG

topics.title: Act I: The Mathematics of the City

concepts.title: Seven Bridges, One Sunday Walk: What a Graph Actually Is
concepts.summary: Euler's move on the bridges of Königsberg — discard geometry, keep connectivity — is the same move that turns a corpus into a knowledge graph.

concepts.title: The Adjacency Matrix: Where a Graph Becomes Calculable
concepts.summary: Numbering the vertices and recording edges as a matrix turns a drawing into something you can compute with — degree, walk counts, and every algorithm that follows.

concepts.title: Two Kinds of Randomness: Erdős–Rényi versus Barabási
concepts.summary: Fair-coin random graphs have no hubs; real networks do, because they grow by preferential attachment — and every knowledge graph inherits the same heavy tail.

concepts.title: Small Worlds and the Fractal-but-Real City
concepts.summary: Short paths plus tight clustering make a small world, and knowledge inherits the same self-similar, communities-within-communities architecture at a handful of real levels.

concepts.title: Communities, Modularity, and the Algorithm to Remember
concepts.summary: Modularity measures density-over-chance; Louvain optimizes it fast but can leave disconnected communities, and Leiden is the fix that Microsoft GraphRAG runs verbatim.

concepts.title: The Laplacian: One Definition, and a Door Left Ajar
concepts.summary: L = D − A measures how rough a score looks across a graph's edges — the same smoothing operator that reappears this afternoon as personalized PageRank.

topics.title: Act II: The Web of Knowledge — Triplets, Types, and Three Layers

concepts.title: Knowledge Is an Interconnected Web: Triplets and Their Types
concepts.summary: A knowledge graph is a bag of head-relation-tail triplets, and every fact triplet has a schema triplet standing behind it — the three-layer reading a corpus can be given.

concepts.title: Who Extracts: The Scooby-Doo Problem and Generic-Entity Hubs
concepts.summary: LLM extraction is cheap but indiscriminate, and the generic entities it inflates — United States, Person, Protein — become exactly the hubs Act I predicted, now with a name.

topics.title: Act III: The Many Meanings of GraphRAG

concepts.title: From Neighbor Expansion to Microsoft GraphRAG
concepts.summary: The oldest GraphRAG walks two hops from query entities and floods on hubs; Microsoft's 2024 pipeline instead harvests communities — at a real invoice.

concepts.title: The In-Betweens: LazyGraphRAG, LightRAG, and HippoRAG
concepts.summary: Three successors answer the invoice by deferring, slimming, or replacing community detection with personalized PageRank — the last one foreshadows tonight's centerpiece.

concepts.title: MemGraphRAG: Three Diseases and a Shared Memory
concepts.summary: MemGraphRAG diagnoses isolated fragment-level extraction as GraphRAG's root defect, then builds its graph by promoting only schemas whose frequency clears a threshold.

concepts.title: The Experiment: Running the Paper on Itself
concepts.summary: Running MemGraphRAG's own construction pipeline on a dozen passages of the paper itself produced a staircase of thresholds where no rung admits signal without noise.

concepts.title: Retrieval Without Communities: Three Cities of Lights and the Honey
concepts.summary: MemGraphRAG scores each layer's embeddings against the query, then lets that semantic energy diffuse via personalized PageRank — the Laplacian's diffusion, leashed and named.

concepts.title: Three Critiques, One Disease: Preserve, Then Decide
concepts.summary: MemGraphRAG indicts isolated extraction for destroying information, then commits the same sin three times at construction time — the fix is to defer judgment to query time.

topics.title: The Practitioner's Ledger: Patterns, Anti-Patterns, and the Sidecar

concepts.title: The Practitioner's Ledger: Patterns, Anti-Patterns, and the Sidecar
concepts.summary: GraphRAG is always a sidecar, never a replacement — it earns its keep on global sensemaking over a high-value sub-corpus, routed there by a local-versus-global query classifier.

weeks.title: The Two Gates of the Gatehouse: Guardrails, Grounding, Refusal & Humility

topics.title: Act I: The Gatehouse — Keeping Bad Questions Out

concepts.title: Two Gates, Two Virtues: Why RAG Needs Both
concepts.summary: A guardrailed RAG system needs two different gates guarding two different failures — a front gate that faces an adversary, and an exit gate that faces its own sincere machine.

concepts.title: Family A — Malformed and Evasive Input
concepts.summary: The model reads far more than your filters do, so an attacker who wants past a toxicity classifier simply encodes the message the more capable reader downstream will decode and obey.

concepts.title: Family B — Adversarial Intent
concepts.summary: There is no clean boundary between data and instructions in one token stream, so every prompt-injection defense is a way of re-drawing a boundary the architecture never had.

concepts.title: The RAG-Native Threat: Indirect Injection via Poisoned Retrieval
concepts.summary: The malicious instruction can lie dormant inside a document rather than the query, so the attacker never has to get past your gate at all — only into your index.

concepts.title: Family C — Access and Identity
concepts.summary: A query can be polite, on-topic, and injection-free and still be one this particular person must never have answered, because the failure is authorization, not content.

concepts.title: Family D — Abuse, Economics, and the Cheapest Structural Gate
concepts.summary: The last request-side family needs no forbidden word at all — it abuses the system by using it too much, spending its wallet, or exploiting its credulity — and one comparison operator, the length cap, retires most of it before a single classifier runs.

concepts.title: Giving the Gate a Memory: Duplicates, Keyword Stuffing, and Frustration
concepts.summary: Every gate so far judges one query in isolation and forgets it instantly — but a whole class of pattern, from repeated jailbreak attempts to a frustrated user, is only visible across a sequence of queries.

concepts.title: The Cheap First Gate: Domain Classification and the Toxicity Layer
concepts.summary: One cheap classifier asking 'is this even about our domain?' silently absorbs most off-topic malice for free, and a dedicated toxicity layer catches the on-topic malice the domain gate cannot see.

concepts.title: The False-Positive Tax, and Orchestrating the Gatehouse
concepts.summary: A suspicious posture is right at any single gate, but false-positive rates compound across a deep stack until the gatehouse quietly turns away one legitimate user in six.

topics.title: Act II: The Conscience — Keeping Bad Answers In

concepts.title: The Wizard's Curtain: Groundedness, Faithfulness, and the RAGAS Triad
concepts.summary: A RAG system speaks in the same confident voice whether or not there's real evidence behind it, so groundedness measures — claim by claim — whether the confidence was earned.

concepts.title: The Assertion–Evidence Bipartite Graph
concepts.summary: Turning the faithfulness definition into a graph — claims on one side, evidence on the other — turns a vague verdict of 'this answer seems off' into a pointer at the exact offending sentence.

concepts.title: Two Verifiers and the Escalation Ladder of Conscience
concepts.summary: An LLM judge is smarter than the cheap NLI model but carries its own documented biases, so production conscience is a cost-ordered cascade that spends the expensive verifier only on the residue the cheap one couldn't settle.

concepts.title: Citation Faithfulness, Caught Hallucinations, and Who Guards the Guard
concepts.summary: A citation is itself a claim that can be false — and detecting a hallucination is worthless without a policy for what to do with it, which is where Act II confronts the recursive limits of its own machinery.

topics.title: Act III: Refusal and Humility

concepts.title: Refusal Is a First-Class Output: The Three Doors, and Why Humility Is Graded
concepts.summary: Sometimes the honest output is no output at all — but refusal is a binary values decision through one of three doors, while humility is the graded, epistemic skill of saying how much of the rest is actually known.

concepts.title: Verbalized Uncertainty: The Linguistics of an Honest Hedge
concepts.summary: A hedge is only honest if a real, measured signal sits underneath it — which rules out both a fake-precise confidence number and the model's own self-report of how sure it is.

concepts.title: Conformal Abstention, Calibration, and the Positive Conscience
concepts.summary: Conformal prediction turns a raw uncertainty score into a threshold with a provable, distribution-free error-rate guarantee — and the whole ethic of the week is stating that error rate out loud instead of guessing at it.

topics.title: Laboratory Sessions

concepts.title: Laboratory Sessions: What We Build and Measure
concepts.summary: Eight labs turn this week's intuition into a deployed artifact in front of a real RAG system, building the gatehouse first, then the conscience, then the honest refusal — and measuring every detector rather than trusting it on faith.
